about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Croque Madame
recipes.summary: Toasted ham and gruyere sandwiches under a creamy cheese sauce, topped with a fried egg.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a tray with baking paper. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Season with nutmeg and salt.
Top 4 slices of bread with the ham and half the gruyere, then close the sandwiches with the other slices. Place on the tray and spread each with the white sauce.
Scatter the remaining gruyere on top and bake for 12 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Fry the eggs in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and place one on each sandwich.
notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Use sliced bread that is a day old if you can, as it holds the sauce better.

recipes.title: Galette Complète (Buckwheat Crepes with Ham, Egg and Gruyere)
recipes.summary: Lacy buckwheat crepes folded around ham, melted gruyere and a soft egg.
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour, 1 egg, water and salt in a bowl until smooth, then melt 20g of the butter and whisk it in.

Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat and brush with a little butter. Pour in a quarter of the batter and swirl to coat. Cook for 2 minutes, until the edges lift and the base is crisp, then flip.
Scatter a quarter of the ham and gruyere in the centre, crack an egg on top and cook for 4 minutes, until the white is set and the cheese has melted.
Fold in the four sides to make a square, slide onto a plate and repeat with the remaining batter and filling.
notes: Food safety: cook the egg until the white is fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free: buckwheat flour is gluten-free but check the packet for cross-contamination.

recipes.title: Boeuf en Daube Provençale
recipes.summary: Beef braised for hours with red wine, orange peel, tomato and olives, in the style of Provence.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy casserole over high heat in batches for 4 minutes each, until deep brown. Set aside.
Cook the pancetta, onion and carrot in the same pot for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and boil for 5 minutes, until reduced by a third. Return the beef, add the tomatoes, orange peel, thyme and bay leaves and bring to a simmer.
Cover and bake for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender, adding the olives for the last 15 minutes. Season to taste.
notes: Food safety: braised beef is tender at around 90°C inside. Cool leftovers within an hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days; it improves on day two.
Gluten-free. Serve with creamy mash or buttered pasta.

recipes.title: Poulet Rôti à l'Ail (Roast Chicken with Whole Garlic)
recipes.summary: Roast chicken scented with thyme and lemon, surrounded by soft, sweet cloves of garlic and crisp potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the chicken all over with the butter and salt, then put the lemon and half the thyme in the cavity.
Scatter the potatoes, onion, garlic and remaining thyme in a roasting tin and sit the chicken on top. Pour the wine into the tin.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear, turning the potatoes once.
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with the potatoes, squeezing the soft garlic from its skins.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh, with clear juices. Rest it for 15 minutes.
Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Tartiflette-Style Potato Bake
recipes.summary: Sliced potatoes baked with bacon, onion, white wine and melting soft cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the potato slices in salted water for 8 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Cook the bacon and onion in the oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes, until reduced.
Layer half the potato in a baking dish, scatter with half the bacon mixture and half the cheese. Repeat, then pour the cream over the top.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until browned and serve the dish piping hot; refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Traditionally made with reblochon; gruyere melts just as well.

recipes.title: Fish Meunière with Lemon Butter and Baby Potatoes
recipes.summary: Flour-dusted white fish fillets pan-fried in butter and finished with lemon, parsley and capers.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until tender, then drain and keep warm.

Season the fish and dust lightly with the flour. Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the fish for 3 minutes each side, until golden and opaque all the way through. Lift onto plates.
Add the remaining butter to the pan and cook for 2 minutes, until it smells nutty and is golden brown. Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, capers and parsley.
Spoon the butter over the fish and serve with the potatoes.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Use any firm white fish such as snapper, flathead or whiting.

recipes.title: Quiche Lorraine
recipes.summary: A buttery homemade pastry case filled with bacon, gruyere and a silky egg and cream custard.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs, then mix in the egg and iced water until a dough forms. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), roll the dough out to fit a 23cm tart tin, prick the base with a fork and bake with baking paper and weights for 15 minutes, until pale golden. Remove the paper and weights and bake for 5 minutes more.
Fry the bacon in a pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until golden, and scatter over the pastry with the gruyere.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and a pinch of salt and pour over the filling. Reduce the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Bake for 30 minutes, until the filling is set with a slight wobble in the centre. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
notes: Food safety: the custard must be set and the centre hot (at least 72°C). Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Good served warm or cold.

recipes.title: Frittata di Pasta (Italian Pasta Frittata)
recipes.summary: A thick, golden omelette studded with spaghetti, peas and herbs, sliced like a cake.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water for 8 minutes, adding the peas for the last minute, then drain and cut roughly with scissors.
Beat the eggs with the cheese, parsley, salt and pepper and stir in the pasta and peas.
Heat the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat, pour in the mixture and cook for 8 minutes, until the base is golden and the edge is set.
Slide onto a plate, flip back into the pan and cook for 5 minutes, until the centre is firm. Cut into wedges.
notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully firm; refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within 2 days.
Vegetarian; good warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Ricotta and Honey Toast with Pear and Walnuts
recipes.summary: Thick sourdough toast spread with creamy ricotta, sliced pear, toasted walnuts and honey.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Stir the lemon zest into the ricotta and spread thickly over the toast.
Top with the pear slices and walnuts and drizzle with the honey.
notes: Vegetarian.
Ripe, juicy pears work best; swap in figs when in season.

recipes.title: Sweet Polenta Porridge with Cinnamon Apples and Almonds
recipes.summary: Creamy polenta cooked in milk and served with buttery spiced apple and crunchy almonds.
steps: Bring the milk, water and honey to a gentle simmer in a saucepan, then whisk in the polenta in a thin stream. Cook, stirring often, for 10 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the apple with the cinnamon for 5 minutes, until soft and golden.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the apple and almonds.
notes: Vegetarian and gluten-free.
Loosen with a splash of hot milk if it thickens as it stands.

recipes.title: Egg Bruschetta with Roasted Tomatoes and Ricotta
recipes.summary: Garlic-rubbed sourdough topped with blistered cherry tomatoes, ricotta and a fried egg.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the tomatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt in a tin and roast for 12 minutes, until blistered and bursting.
Rub the toasted bread with the cut garlic and spread with the ricotta, until evenly covered.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Pile the tomatoes on the bread, top with the eggs and basil, then serve right away.
notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.
